B Transformer II Electromagnetic Induction
C Resonance phenomenon to occur III Quality factor
D Sharpness of resonance IV Mutual Inductance

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A) An AC generator works on the electromagnetic induction principle. So, A→II

(B) The transformer works on the principle of mutual induction. So, B→IV

(C) Resonance occurs when the value of inductive and capacitive reactance have equal magnitude but a phase difference of 180°.  So, C→I

(D) The sharpness of resonance is defined using the quality factor which explains how fast energy decay in an oscillating system. D→III

options: Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is false but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is true
Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are true
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is true but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is false

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula for impedance is given by 

Z=R2+XL-XC2

At resonance, XL=XC. So, Zmin=R

Power will be maximum when impedance is minimum. Thus the maximum power occurs in a purely resistive circuit.

questions.q:
As per the given graph, choose the correct representation for curve A and curve B
{Where XC= Reactance of pure capacitive circuit connected with A.C. source
XL= Reactance of pure inductive circuit connected with A.C. source
R= Impedance of pure resistive circuit connected with A.C. source
Z= Impedance of the LCR series circuit }
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the inductive reactance is

XL=ωL   ...1

The formula to calculate capacitive reactance is

XC=1ωC   ...2

As can be seen from equation (1), the inductive reactance varies directly with the frequency and equation (2) indicates that capacitive reactance varies inversely with the frequency.

Hence, curve A represents the capacitive reactance and curve B represents the inductive reactance.
